title: Verify invalid tank-volume curves across file loading and API updates
problem: The real pinned library accepts decreasing and interior-dip water-storage volume curves through file loading, API assignment and later curve edits. Direct decreasing assignment returns a NaN diameter without an API error; increasing requested depth yields decreasing initial volume. No process crash or operational consequence is established.
humanitarian_relevance: Clear validation may improve reliability of water-network analysis tools. No measured effect on drinking-water safety, utility decisions or resource use.

evidence.claim: Reporter says invalid tank-volume curves can produce decreasing volume while filling and a floating-point exception when negative area is converted to diameter. These runtime claims have not been independently reproduced.

Pinned file initialization and two API assignment routes derive area from endpoint slope. Curve point/bulk setters check increasing X but not Y; generic decreasing pump curves must remain valid. Existing curve/node tests inspected, not run.

Thirty-four native-library cases pass as current-behavior assertions across GPM/LPS units, three curve shapes and five entry paths, plus cylindrical and decreasing-pump controls. All open/assignment/hydraulic-initialization calls succeed. Direct decreasing assignment yields NaN diameter; interior dips and subsequent edits retain finite diameter while volume decreases with greater requested depth. Metric EN_VOLCURVE assignment also yields 0.3048 times the diameter from file/EN_settankdata routes for the same valid curve. All 144 tracked source files remain byte-identical before build and after probes.

The unchanged native CMake baseline passes: 88 Boost cases across six binaries, plus two threaded runs returning status zero. All six CTest entries pass and the unregistered string-helper binary passes separately. All 34 behavior cases pass again against the test-enabled library; 144 tracked files remain byte-identical. Bounded searches found historical unit-changing/parameter issues, but not a matching report of the fixed-unit EN_VOLCURVE nominal-diameter discrepancy.

Twelve four-hour native hydraulic simulations compare fixed-unit file/EN_VOLCURVE/EN_settankdata routes before/after save-reload. The metric saved row contains the smaller nominal diameter, but reloading recomputes it. Levels, volumes, flow and pressure agree up to floating-point differences (maximum absolute difference 1.82e-12 in volume). No consequential hydraulic effect is established for these two synthetic networks.

code_surface: At dev 83e25bbe2b0b460803e71df03bc989afe9557ea3: src/input1.c inittanks; src/input2.c parser; src/validate.c validatetanks/validatecurves; src/epanet.c public tank assignment, curve mutation and getters. Existing tests/test_curve.cpp and tests/test_node.cpp located. Real C library exercised through public API; no copied-function simulation.
proposed_change: First reproduce invalid-data handling through the real library and agree scope. Consider consistent tank-specific validation across relevant entry points only after maintainer confirmation; preserve generic/pump curve semantics and document errors/rollback.
tests: All six registered CTest programs pass: 86 unchanged Boost cases plus a threaded program whose two EPANET runs each report status zero. The separately run, unregistered string-helper binary adds two cases, for 88 Boost cases across six binaries and seven executables overall. All 34 native-library behavior cases pass against the test-enabled library; all 144 tracked source files remain unchanged. No added production regression/fix or real-world operational validation. A further 12 four-hour native runs compare route and save/reload behavior on two valid synthetic networks; no meaningful hydraulic difference is observed.
environment: Pinned native Release build with BUILD_TESTS=ON, CMake 3.31.6, Apple Clang 21.0.0 and isolated Boost 1.85.0. Official Boost archive SHA256 verified; selected test/system/thread/filesystem plus chrono/atomic components built locally with no global installation, inherited credentials or user/site build configuration. 88 Boost cases, two successful threaded runs and 34 native behavior cases pass; 144 tracked target files unchanged. No external services or operational-system access.
maintainer: Verified local evidence is ready for a concise #883 scope inquiry. No upstream message has been sent, no bot eligibility or scope confirmed, and no review date is invented. The current compute-governance human-review requirement applies to the prepared draft; existing GitHub communication authorization is not revoked.
risks: Original invalid water-storage curves remain accepted; their production consequence and desired error/rollback policy are unconfirmed. The separate valid-curve metric discrepancy affects returned/saved diameter but showed no meaningful hydraulic effect in 12 bounded simulations and corrects on reload. Do not promote it as a consequential simulation bug or expand #883 silently. Quality/mixing and other diameter uses remain untested; no independent human review or bot eligibility is claimed.
